# Aparinipphannakathā (Kv 23.5)

**ID:** Kv 23.5  
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Aparinipphannakathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul30.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul30.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aparinipphannakathā* is the fifth controversy of the twenty-third chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. According to the commentary and modern studies, the controversy addresses a view attributed to the Uttarāpathakas and the Hetuvādins [Dube 1980; Bareau 1955]. Basing their position on the canonical verses of the nun Vajirā—which declare that it is suffering (*dukkha*) alone that arises and ceases—these schools maintained that *dukkha* alone is determined (*parinipphanna* / *parfait*), whereas all other aggregates (*khandha*), sense spheres (*āyatana*), elements (*dhātu*), and faculties (*indriya*) are undetermined or unproduced (*aparinipphanna* / *imparfait*) [Dube 1980; Bareau 1955; Hazra 1994]. In the debate, the Theravādin interlocutor refutes this view by arguing that the scope of *parinipphanna* is not exhausted by *dukkha* proper, and because phenomena other than Nibbāna are causally conditioned (*paṭiccasamuppanna*), other constituents of mind and matter cannot be considered unproduced or uncaused [Dube 1980; Aung and Rhys Davids 1915].

- [Bareau 1955] André Bareau, Les sectes bouddhiques du Petit Véhicule (1955) — Listing of the Uttarāpathaka thesis that aggregates, elements, and faculties are aparinipphanna.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Summary of the proposition that all save ill is undetermined.
